guides.content:
Buying headphones is easy to get wrong: the best-sounding pair is useless if it hurts after an hour. Start with fit, then check the specs that matter.

## 1. Pick the right style
Over-ear headphones are best for long sessions at home or in the office — bigger drivers, better noise cancelling, and they do not sit inside your ear. Earbuds are better for travel, workouts and calls on the go. If you wear glasses, try over-ear pads that are soft and deep.

## 2. Battery and charging
For over-ear headphones, 30+ hours of battery is good and 40+ is excellent. For earbuds, look at the total with the case (20+ hours), not just one charge. Fast charging — 10 minutes for a few hours of playback — is genuinely useful.

## 3. Noise cancelling: do you need it?
Active noise cancelling (ANC) is worth paying for if you fly, commute, or work in a noisy room. If you mostly listen at home, a good pair without ANC often sounds just as good for less money.

## 4. Check the price, not just the discount
A big "was" price means nothing on its own. Compare the current price with similar models, read real reviews about comfort, and check the "Price as of" date on ZayPick — Amazon prices change often, so always confirm the current price on Amazon before you buy.

guides.content:
An air fryer earns its counter space only if it fits your household and is easy to clean. Here is how to choose one.

## 1. Size first
A 3–4L basket suits couples and small households. For a family of four or more, go 5L or bigger — a basket that is too small means cooking in two batches, every single time.

## 2. The basket matters more than the presets
Look for a non-stick, dishwasher-safe basket that slides out smoothly. You will clean it after every use, so this is the feature you will notice daily. Presets are handy but not essential; reliable temperature control matters more.

## 3. Wattage and counter space
Most good air fryers are 1,400–1,800W. Measure your counter before you buy — including the space behind it, because the basket pulls out towards you. Also check the cord length and where your nearest socket is.

## 4. What to cook first
Fries, chicken wings, vegetables and reheated leftovers are where an air fryer shines. It will not replace your oven for big roasts, but for everyday meals it is faster and uses less energy.

## Our pick on ZayPick

guides.content:
Your first running shoes should be comfortable from the first run, not after "breaking them in". Here is what actually matters.

## 1. Buy for comfort, not looks
Try your normal size first. Most running shoes run true to size, but some brands run narrow — if your toes touch the front, go half a size up. There should be a thumb's width between your longest toe and the front of the shoe.

## 2. Cushioning beats weight for beginners
A soft, cushioned sole protects your knees while you build up distance. Lightweight racing shoes feel fast but offer less protection. Start with a versatile cushioned trainer and upgrade later, once you know your gait.

## 3. Rotate and replace on time
Replace running shoes after roughly 500–800 km, or when the cushioning feels flat and the outsole is worn smooth. If you run three or more times a week, a second pair lets each pair dry out and last longer.

## 4. Where to buy
Buy from a seller with easy returns, so you can try them indoors first. Prices on Amazon change often — check the "Price as of" date on ZayPick and confirm the current price on Amazon before you buy.
